text:
Just opened a new business? Get on Google first.

Set up your Google Business Profile. Right main category. Real photos. Verified.

Google even lets you add an opening date up to 90 days ahead, so you can be on the map before the doors open.

What can SEO actually do for your business?

Put you in front of people at the exact moment they need you.

Power's out at 7am. Someone types "electrician Glenorchy".
They want someone today. They'll ring whoever's at the top.

SEO decides if that's you.

Easiest content plan for a local business:

Write down the questions customers ask you every week.

"How long does a bathroom reno take?"
"Do I need council approval?"

Answer each one properly on your website.

Next few pages sorted.

Just opened a barber shop in Hamilton, Newcastle and the phone's quiet?

SEO for a new business takes months to build.

Google Ads can put you in front of people searching "barber Hamilton" this week.

I'd run both. The ads pay the bills while the map listing builds.

A 12-month lock-in with a marketer is like a mechanic keeping your car keys until next year.

If the work's good, you'll come back anyway.
If the work's poor, you should be free to go.

That's why I don't do lock-ins. Not working? You stop.

Simple.

Google says it ranks local businesses on three things: relevance, distance and prominence.

You can't move your shop closer to every customer.

SEO works on the other two. Clear pages on what you do. A complete profile. Reviews that show people trust you.

How are yours looking?
